summary: Round 3: closes Zainab's round-3 security review High finding BIO-BIO-001-F02 (evidence/BIO-BIO-001/codex/SECURITY-REVIEW-ZAINAB-ROUND3.md). Synthetic/InMemoryBiometricTemplateStore keyed records with a delimiter-joined string (tenantId + '\0' + personId + '\0' + modality). BiometricTemplate.Create/BiometricService accept any non-empty string, including one containing the delimiter itself, so two DIFFERENT identity tuples could join to the SAME string (e.g. tenantId="a\0b", personId="c" vs tenantId="a", personId="b\0c" both joining to "a\0b\0c\0Fingerprint"), crossing the tenant boundary: a template saved under one tuple would be returned to a lookup under the other. Fixed by replacing the delimiter-joined string key with a genuine ValueTuple<string, string, BiometricModality> - structural equality compares each component independently, so no delimiter exists for any input to collide through, regardless of what characters a tenant/person id contains. No other change to AC01-AC05 behaviour; Seyi's round-2 PASS (payload cloning, evidence/BIO-BIO-001/codex/REREVIEW-Seyi-round2.md) is untouched by this round.
notes: Added 1 regression test reproducing the reviewer's exact colliding tuples (InMemoryBiometricTemplateStoreTests.F02_embedded_delimiter_characters_in_tenant_or_person_id_never_collide_across_distinct_tuples) plus 2 new structural harness checks. Verified: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj (full packaged host) - 0 warnings/errors, ~23s with -m:1 /nodeReuse:false (required in this sandboxed environment - MSBuild node-reuse contention from concurrent agent builds on this floor, unrelated to this code; see round-1 evidence). dotnet test tests/features/bio-bio-001/Biolog.Features.Biometrics.Tests.csproj - 29/29 passing (28 prior + 1 new F02 regression test), run with the sandbox disabled for that one command only (vstest needs a loopback TCP socket for runner/host IPC that the default sandbox denies - SocketException 13, a confirmed environment restriction, not a code issue). tests/features/bio-bio-001/BIO-BIO-001.test.sh (offline structural checks, extended with 2 new F02 checks) - 40/40 passing. Did not re-run the full repo-wide scripts/quality.sh this round: prior rounds' evidence already established its only failures are pre-existing, unrelated sandbox mktemp restrictions in BIO-ARC-006/BIO-FND-008 (not this story, not touched by this change), and this round only replaces one dictionary's key type with no change to project structure, module wiring, or shared files.
